company: The San Francisco Compute Company (SF Compute)

ownership.quote: Founded in 2023, the company recently hired Eric Park, former CEO of AI cloud provider Voltage Park, as CTO.

stage.quote: SF Compute has secured $40 million in a Series A equity financing round for the expansion of its AI compute marketplace.
stage.note: No accelerator found for SF Compute itself; searches of the YC company directory turned up no match (an earlier Evan Conrad startup, not SF Compute, had informal ties to Y Combinator people — rejected as not applicable to this provider).

total_funding_usd.basis: Sum of the $12M seed (company's own LinkedIn/hiring post, Jan 2025) and the $40M Series A (WSJ/DataCenterDynamics, Nov 2025). Note: Tracxn's aggregate figure states total funding of only "$40M over 2 rounds," which appears to undercount the seed and disagrees with the primary-source seed amount; we use the sum of the two independently confirmed rounds.
total_funding_usd.quote: We raised a $12 million seed round led by Jack Altman (Alt Capital) with participation from Akshay Kothari (Co-founder & COO, Notion), Christina Cacioppo (Co-founder & CEO, Vanta), Terrence Rohan (Otherwise Fund), Noah Smith, and many others.

last_round.quote: The funding round was led by DCVC and Wing Venture Capital. It also saw participation from existing backers, including Electric Capital and Alt Capital.

note: Independent, venture-backed startup founded in 2023 by Evan Conrad (CEO) and co-founders including Ethan W. Anderson (COO); two products under one brand — the SF Compute GPU orderbook/marketplace and the newer Autoresearch sandbox/node platform this card's pricing centers on. Series A (Nov 2025) valued the company at $300M post-money per WSJ. No Y Combinator or other accelerator affiliation found for SF Compute itself.
